nodes.name: Anodic nitrate intercalation
nodes.procedure: The graphite substrate was first subjected to anodic treatment at 20 mA cm⁻² for 600 s to allow NO₃⁻ intercalation.
nodes.source_text: In a typical synthesis, the graphite substrate was first subjected to anodic treatment at 20 mA cm⁻² for 600 s to allow NO₃⁻ intercalation

nodes.name: Ni-Ce co-electrodeposition on graphite
nodes.procedure: The nitrate-inserted graphite substrate was applied to cathodic deposition at -20 mA cm⁻² for 600 s in a 50 ml electrolytic bath containing aqueous nitrate solution with 0.1 M total metal ions (Ni:Ce = 9:1) at 25°C. The bath, graphite plate, and all substrates were ultrasonically cleaned in 1 M HCl and Millipore water (18.2 MΩ cm⁻¹) prior to deposition. A conducting substrate (graphite), graphite plate (counter), and saturated calomel electrode (SCE, reference) served as the three-electrode system.

unit_operations.name: Ultrasonic cleaning
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The bath, graphite plate, and all substrates were ultrasonically cleaned in 1 M HCl and Millipore water

unit_operations.name: Cathodic electrodeposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: applied to a cathodic deposition at -20 mA cm⁻² for 600 s in electrolyte containing totally 0.1 M Ni and Ce nitrates

nodes.source_text: Electrodeposition was performed at 25°C in a 50 ml electrolytic bath... graphite substrate was first subjected to anodic treatment... then applied to a cathodic deposition at -20 mA cm⁻² for 600 s.

nodes.name: Ni(OH)₂ electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Direct cathodic electrodeposition was performed at current of -20 mA cm⁻² for 300 s in 0.1 M nickel nitrate aqueous solution at 25°C.
nodes.source_text: On non-graphitic substrates such as bare GC, CP, NF, and Ti, direct cathodic electrodeposition was performed at current of -20 mA cm⁻² for 300 s.

nodes.name: CeO₂ electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Cathodic electrodeposition performed at -20 mA cm⁻² for 300 s in 0.1 M cerium nitrate aqueous solution at 25°C.
nodes.source_text: Each electrodeposition was performed by applying a constant current density of -20 mA cm⁻² for 300 s in 0.1 M metal nitrate electrolyte

nodes.description: OER performance on RDE with low mass loading (multiple catalysts)
nodes.source_text: Figure 5a shows the representative cyclic voltammograms (CVs) of Ni–Ce hybrid, Ni(OH)₂, CeO₂, and RuO₂ supported on graphite-modified GC electrode in rotating disk electrode (RDE) testing mode... the NiCeOxHy hybrid exhibited a low onset overpotential of 180 mV and required only 207 mV overpotential to reach a current density of 10 mA cm⁻²... mass activity of NiCeOxHy is 406.8 A g⁻¹... specific activity... of NiCeOxHy/G is 2.5 mA cm⁻²

nodes.characterization_summary: Cross-section SEM shows NiCeOxHy firmly supported on graphite without interspace; elemental mapping shows penetration of Ni, Ce, O into graphite.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the generated deposit was firmly supported on the graphite substrate without apparent interspace, as shown in the SEM image (Fig. 3a). Elemental mapping clearly showed penetration of Ni, Ce, and O into graphite (Fig. 3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows NiCeOxHy nanoparticles anchored on graphite layers (Supplementary Fig. 7); deposit consists of ultrasmall crystalline CeO2 nanoparticles (3.5 nm) in amorphous Ni(OH)2 matrix forming mosaic structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The firm deposit–substrate interaction was further evidenced by high-resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) imaging (Supplementary Fig. 7), which showed anchoring of NiCeOxHy nanoparticles on graphite layers.

properties.description: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image labeled b

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD (Supplementary Fig. 14a) indicates NiCeOxHy hybrid consists of ultrasmall crystalline CeO2 nanoparticles and amorphous Ni(OH)2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A combination of HRTEM (Fig. 4b and Supplementary Fig. 13), selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) (Fig. 4b, inset) and XRD (Supplementary Fig. 14a) further indicates that the deposited NiCeOxHy hybrid consists of ultrasmall crystalline CeO2 nanoparticles (typical size 3.5 nm) and amorphous Ni(OH)2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni:Ce atomic ratio of 9:1 estimated for typical NiCeOxHy hybrid sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In a typical hybrid sample, a Ni:Ce atomic ratio of 9:1 was estimated by energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) (Supplementary Fig. 14b).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCeOxHy shows bands at 3425 and 1630 cm⁻¹ (absorbed water), 1385 cm⁻¹ (NO₃⁻), broad band ~3500 cm⁻¹ and weak peak at 1296 cm⁻¹ (–OH stretching); Ni–OH bending vibration blue shifted by ~13 cm⁻¹ relative to Ni(OH)2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FTIR spectra of the Ni, Ce, and Ni–Ce deposits (Fig. 4c) present bands at 3425 and 1630 cm⁻¹, which are assigned to the stretching modes of absorbed water.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p3/2: Ni(II) 855 eV, Ni(III) 856.4 eV (0.3 eV positive shift vs Ni(OH)2); O 1s: 529 eV (CeO2), 530.6 eV (Ni(OH)2), 531.8 eV (NiOOH), 532.8 eV (H2O); Ce 3d >881 eV (Ce(IV), 0.5 eV negative shift vs pure CeO2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the Ni 2p3/2 spectra (Fig. 4d), both Ni–Ce hybrid and Ni hydroxide contain Ni(II) (at 855 eV) and Ni(III) species (856.4 and 856.1 eV). There is a positive shift of 0.3 eV for Ni(III) in the Ni–Ce hybrid.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCeOxHy shows broad peak 420-520 cm⁻¹ (Ni–O and Ce–O bands) and new vibration at 613 cm⁻¹ evidencing Ni–O–Ce interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra (Supplementary Fig. 16) show a broad peak in the range of 420-520 cm⁻¹, which could be attributed to Ni–O and Ce–O bands.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman on NiCeOxHy/G shows γ-NiOOH formation at 1.27 V (characteristic peaks 474, 554 cm⁻¹), 0.14 V lower than pure Ni(OH)2; α-Ni(OH)2 signals almost undetectable.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the γ-NiOOH phase appears at 1.27 V, 0.14 V lower than the conversion potential of Ni(OH)2. These results indicate that γ-NiOOH is the active phase for the OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando XRD on NiCeOxHy/NF shows pure γ-NiOOH with (003) facets (d=0.69 nm); Ni(OH)2/NF shows mainly γ-NiOOH + minor β-Ni(OH)2 with preferential (006) planes (d=0.34 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the NiCeOxHy electrode, only γ-NiOOH phase is discernable (Fig. 6d)... Note that γ-NiOOH exposes merely (003) facets in NiCeOxHy as compared to the preferential (006) planes in Ni(OH)2. The interplanar spacings of (003) and (006) planes are 0.69 and 0.34 nm, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern confirms crystalline CeO2 nanoparticles in amorphous NiCeOxHy matrix.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A combination of HRTEM (Fig. 4b and Supplementary Fig. 13), selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) (Fig. 4b, inset) and XRD (Supplementary Fig. 14a) further indicates that the deposited NiCeOxHy hybrid consists of ultrasmall crystalline CeO2 nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Thermogravimetric analysis shows water content of 9.9 wt% in NiCeOxHy hybrid.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Thermogravimetric analysis further indicates that water accounts for 9.9 wt% in the NiCeOxHy hybrid (Supplementary Fig. 15).
